Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the fish-control skill and its required references, then inspect the inherited guidance and rollout evidence before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll use the bookshelf only for transferable control invariants and will document any influence in the required note block.

The workspace also provides a wake-visual inspection skill tailored to this exact policy task, so I’m using it to make sure the architecture is grounded in both required 3D views before any edit. I’ll now inventory the inherited notes, sampled metrics/keyframes, and policy variants; only after viewing them will I open the bookshelf primitives and any relevant source family.

The two sheets confirm direct self-propulsion: both retain a compact alternating mid-plane street and localized 3D Lambda2 structures through a nearly straight targetward approach, with no visible wake collapse or boundary-failure precursor. Their terminal paths look almost indistinguishable, so the useful distinction must come from state/action/load and course-margin metrics rather than vortex appearance alone. I’m cross-checking those quantities and the exact policy deltas now.

The cross-check shows a clean but fragile equivalence class: all four capture at the threshold, while terminal body courses remain strongly lateral. The best-score tail-only residual arrives at 15.1403T but has posterior rate pegged at 260°/T and terminal speed about 1.48L/T; drive relief and response-release remain captures but do not improve margin. With the rollout evidence anchored, I’m now consulting the bookshelf primitives for one mechanism-level alternative—not another gain or threshold variant.

The shelf supports one small, compatible mechanism: a near-field approach hold that damps measured slip without suppressing the anterior oscillator or adding persistent bend. I’ll consult the corresponding source notes before translating only that invariant into body-frame closing/miss feedback; species gains, exact phases, and any staged route remain out of scope.

A body-frame reconstruction changes the architectural choice: the prefilled joint-reserve allocator is the current semantic leader even though it is not the score leader. Its final constant-course miss is about 0.362L, versus 0.573–0.651L for the response-release, drive-relief, and tail-only variants; it also crosses mostly targetward at 1.37L/T. I’m preserving that allocation mechanism and checking its sheet plus terminal histories before writing the required pre-edit diagnosis.

The pre-edit hypothesis is now settled: keep the prefilled allocator’s evidenced 0.362L course margin, but make its redirect allocation aware of both joints. When the tail loses reserve, the residual may transfer anteriorly only while the anterior joint also has angle/rate reserve; if neither actuator has reserve, the extra residual fades instead of forcing a new saturation. This is a feedback-structure change, not gain tuning, and leaves the carrier, route, and shared steering unchanged. I’m recording that diagnosis and the reusable evidence lesson before touching the policy.

The single candidate now implements dual-reserve allocation: it changes only the transfer of the existing terminal residual, leaving propulsion, geometry feedback, and the acceleration envelope intact. I’m moving into deterministic checks now—schema/contract, reflection symmetry, finite bounded actions, and confirmation that the new gate is active—then I’ll run the mandated workspace check runner and repair any failure.

The policy contract and editable-boundary checks pass. The mandated guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` contains the identical “copied to guidance” parent marker twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. I’m removing only that duplicate metadata line, then rerunning the mandated check; no solver surface beyond the candidate is affected.

The guidance checker now passes after the duplicate parent marker repair. I’m stress-testing the candidate across reflected body-frame target/velocity states and joint angle/rate reserve combinations, comparing it directly with the evaluated prefill to verify three things: finite bounded commands, exact reflection equivariance, and a materially active dual-reserve gate only where the anterior transfer lacks capacity.

The algebraic checks pass on 37,500 states: all commands are finite and strictly within the 30 rad/T² smooth envelope, left/right reflection error is exactly zero, all 37 parameter references resolve, and the mechanism differs from the evaluated prefill by up to 1.77 rad/T². A dry replay of all 2,810 prefill states confirms the gate is active on the encountered trajectory; this is only a state replay, not a claim about the new CFD outcome.

I’ve appended the validation boundary to the provenance note without treating dry replay as rollout evidence. I’m doing the final mandated pass now on the completed artifacts: durable-guidance materiality, Julia contract/schema, editable boundary, nonempty single candidate, and a focused diff against the evaluated prefill.

Implemented exactly one dual-reserve target-policy candidate.

- Candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- Reasoning and bookshelf transfer: [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- Reusable evidence lesson: [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:160)

The policy preserves the prefill’s improved 0.362L reconstructed course margin while gating anterior residual transfer by anterior angle/rate reserve.

All required checks pass: guidance materiality, Julia contract/schema, editable boundary, finite bounded commands over 37,500 states, and exact reflection equivariance. Formal CFD was not run.
